outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic diagram of breast anatomy and a classification table showing approximate population-level frequencies of breast cancer subtypes; it does not present experimentally replicated data, so replicate reporting does not apply.
Panel B is a conceptual schematic outlining the study's aim (circadian phenotypes and their relation to drug sensitivity/tumor growth); it contains no data derived from replicates.
Panel C is a schematic illustrating the method of measuring circadian rhythms via luciferase reporters; it does not show actual replicated experimental data.
Panel D shows illustrative example traces (Model #1-3) to depict the analysis workflow, not actual quantified replicate data.
Panel E is a schematic correlation heatmap illustrating the analysis concept, not an actual result derived from replicated measurements.
Panel F depicts illustrative example growth curves (Model 1-3) to explain the live-imaging/growth quantification workflow, not actual replicated experimental data.
Panel G shows illustrative example dose-response curves to explain the drug sensitivity workflow, not actual data from replicated experiments.

Panel H is a schematic illustrating the genomic analysis workflow using publicly available datasets (gene expression/mutation heatmaps as icons), not primary replicated experimental data generated by this study.

Panel I is a schematic illustration of the concept of defining circadian-based cellular subtypes via PCA/clustering, presented as a conceptual diagram rather than an actual dataset with reported replicate numbers.
